claim: Arctic permafrost soils hold roughly twice as much carbon as the atmosphere; as they thaw, microbes release it as carbon dioxide and methane.

beats.caption: Frozen ground holds twice the sky's carbon
beats.vo: Frozen ground holds twice the sky's carbon.

beats.caption: Permafrost: frozen 2+ years
beats.vo: Permafrost is ground frozen for at least two years. Across the Arctic it locks away over a trillion tons of carbon, about twice what's in the air.

beats.caption: Thaw wakes microbes. They eat the carbon.
beats.vo: That carbon is dead plant matter that froze before it could rot. When the ground thaws, microbes wake up and eat it, and release carbon dioxide and methane.

beats.caption: A freezer that is slowly thawing
beats.vo: That adds greenhouse gas to a warming planet, which can thaw even more ground. Permafrost is a carbon freezer, and the door is slowly opening.

sources.text: NSIDC, Frozen Ground and Permafrost: permafrost is ground frozen for at least two years. https://nsidc.org/learn/parts-cryosphere/frozen-ground-permafrost

NSIDC, 'Plotting the big thaw' (2011): some 1,672 gigatons of carbon in permafrost, more than twice the carbon in the atmosphere; decay releases carbon dioxide and methane. https://nsidc.org/ru/node/31816
NASA Goddard, 'New Arctic Lakes Could Soon Be a Major Source of Atmospheric Methane': thawing permafrost wakes microbes that consume once-frozen organic material.
